name: claude-abort
purpose: The caller cancels mid-stream against CLAUDE: the backend must tear the upstream connection down, which the recorder observes as a client disconnect. This source cancels through its own AbortController bound to the client socket (chat-completions.js:241-245), a different mechanism from the shared path's, so it needs its own recorded case.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.reason: The scenario supplies a synthetic key; the header's presence is the contract, the value is not. CLAUDE authenticates with x-api-key rather than an Authorization bearer.

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>
tier2.reason: API_CLAUDE is a hardcoded literal and this drive sets no reverse_proxy, so the pinned leg reaches the recorder through the probe transport redirect and the Go leg through its seam. The PATH (/v1/messages) is untouched and IS compared.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
